name: Astra centre kit cell 5 (r1 c1)
label: monster_overworld/astra-centre-kit-5 (칸 2229)
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (2/4)

surfaces.part: framed panel with cream interior and pink flower motif

answer.evidence: The cell fills the full 16x16 square (width 16 on every row). It looks like a corner of a flat framed panel: a teal strip on the left, a navy and brown frame running along the top and left, and a cream interior holding a pink flower and green leaf. The column scans show only vertical stacks of frame bands and interior fill. There is no ellipse, no sloped roof or awning plane, and no edge line followed by eave shadow. Rows 2-3 are the brown frame's top edge, which is a 1-2 row rim rather than a top surface. The whole cell reads as a face-on vertical panel with no horizontal surface, so it is a front elevation. It does not look like a gate, pavilion or building with a roof or lintel top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate on the right of the magenta bar is a tiny fragment, about one tile (roughly 18x20 source px). It shows a teal strip beside a pink/white patch, with no roof, walls, door or windows. The references are whole buildings with scalloped tile roofs, timber or stone walls and doors, so this is not the same kind at the same scale. The measured facts do not fault it: 17 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% near-neutral dark edges, which means tinted outlines. But the whole piece uses only 17 distinct colours, against 185 and 66 for the references. At this size I can see only about 3 distinct shading steps on any material, against about 6 on the references' roof ramps. I cannot confirm per-tile roof highlights, plaster speckle or stone-by-stone shading. A single cell cannot be judged as a complete building, and when in doubt the rule is fail.

surfaces.part: brown-framed white panel with pink flower and leaf

answer.evidence: The tile is 16 px wide for all 16 rows. The scan shows a teal strip at x=4, a navy line at rows 0-1, a brown frame at rows 2-3, then a white interior with a pink flower and green leaf. This reads as a flat face-on framed panel, like a picture or window insert. No horizontal band ends in a front-edge line with eave shadow, no ellipse is visible, there is no sloped roof or awning, and no contents are visible inside an open container. The brown rows 2-3 are a frame border, not a top surface. The cell is not a gate, pavilion or building with a roof or lintel top slope, so the structure kind fits poorly. Overall it is a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate on the right of the magenta bar is a tiny icon-sized sprite: a teal bar beside a small pink and white block with a green mark. It has no readable roof, walls, door or windows, so it is not a whole building like the references, which show tiled roofs with per-tile highlights, timber framing, plaster speckle and stone shaded one by one. The measured facts are 17 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edges, so the outline is tinted. These numbers look fine, but at this size they come from a few distinct palette pixels and do not show the multi-step material ramps, roof scallops or wall texture of a building. By eye the piece is much thinner and flatter than either reference, and I cannot accept it as a building next to them. Failing as the wrong kind and structurally shallow, since the numbers alone cannot show it carries the same richness.
